lines.text: Nigeria got its name from a newspaper article, written by a journalist who wasn't even Nigerian.
In 1897, a British journalist named Flora Shaw wrote in The Times of London.
She suggested the name Nigeria, after the mighty River Niger that flows through the land.
Flora later married Frederick Lugard, the colonial official who ruled the territory.
In 1914, Lugard joined the Northern and Southern Protectorates into one country, and the name stuck.
On October first, 1960, Nigeria became independent, and kept the name.
